bibl.title: A Survey on Deep Learning in Medical Image Analysis

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: From the 308 papers reviewed in this survey, it is evident that deep learning has pervaded every aspect of medical image analysis.

span.label: deep learning in medical image analysis
span.quote: Deep learning algorithms, in particular convolutional networks, have rapidly become a methodology of choice for analyzing medical images.

span.label: review
span.quote: This paper reviews the major deep learning concepts pertinent to medical image analysis and summarizes over 300 contributions to the field, most of which appeared in the last year.

span.label: open challenges and future-research directions remain in the field
span.quote: a critical discussion of open challenges and directions for future research

span.label: The survey deliberately excludes traditional (non-deep) feature-learning approaches applied to medical images.
span.quote: In this survey, we focus particularly on such deep models, and do not include the more traditional feature learning approaches that have been applied to medical images.

span.label: Coverage has a hard cut-off date, so later work is not included.
span.quote: The last update to the included papers was on February 1, 2017.

span.label: Completeness of the literature search is an expectation rather than a guarantee.
span.quote: We expect the search terms used to cover most, if not all, of the work incorporating deep learning methods.

span.label: On a widely used dataset the disputed annotations outnumber the agreed ones three to one.
span.quote: dataset pulmonary nodules were annotated by four radiologists independently. Subsequently the readers reviewed each others annotations but no consensus was forced. It turned out that the number of nodules they did not unanimously agreed on to be a nodule, was three times larger than the number they did fully agree on

span.label: Label noise is worse in this field than in the field the methods came from, and the survey says so.
span.quote: Even when data is annotated by domain expert, label noise can be a significant limiting factor in developing algorithms, whereas in computer vision the noise in the labeling of images is typically relatively low

span.label: Training on such data is stated to be an open problem, not a solved preprocessing step.
span.quote: Training a deep learning system on such data requires careful consideration of how to deal with noise and uncertainty in the reference standard. One could think of solutions like incorporating labeling uncertainty directly in the loss function, but this is still an open challenge

span.label: deep convolutional networks, developed in computer vision, adopted as the methodology of choice for medical image analysis (classification, detection, segmentation)
span.quote: Deep learning algorithms, in particular convolutional networks, have rapidly become a methodology of choice for analyzing medical images

span.label: the reference standard - AN ANNOTATION SET WITH ITS DISAGREEMENT LEFT IN: four radiologists annotated independently, reviewed each other, and NO CONSENSUS WAS FORCED, so what every accuracy on this dataset is measured against is a set whose disputed part is three times its agreed part - the standard is not a ground truth but a record of expert disagreement
span.quote: dataset pulmonary nodules were annotated by four radiologists independently. Subsequently the readers reviewed each others annotations but no consensus was forced. It turned out that the number of nodules they did not unanimously agreed on to be a nodule, was three times larger than the number they did fully agree on

span.label: label noise - A FIELD-RELATIVE QUANTITY: the survey contrasts medical imaging, where it can be a significant limiting factor even with domain-expert annotation, against computer vision, where it is typically relatively low - so the same word names a small nuisance in one literature and a limiting factor in the other, and the architectures move between them
span.quote: Even when data is annotated by domain expert, label noise can be a significant limiting factor in developing algorithms, whereas in computer vision the noise in the labeling of images is typically relatively low

span.label: the binary task - A STATED SIMPLIFICATION: normal versus abnormal is called a gross simplification because both classes are highly heterogeneous, which is why systems can excel on common normal subclasses and fail on rare ones; the two-class label is a choice about the data, not a property of it
span.quote: In medical imaging often classification or segmentation is presented as a binary task: normal versus abnormal, object versus background. However, this is often a gross simplification as both classes can be highly heterogeneous

span.label: extends → Shen et al. (2017), the earlier dedicated review of deep learning in medical image analysis
span.quote: Although they cover a substantial amount of work, we feel that important areas of the field were not represented.

span.quote: Some researchers have specifically looked into tackling this imbalance by incorporating intelligence in the training process itself, by applying selective sampling (van Grinsven et al., 2016) or hard negative mining (Wang et al., 2016b). However, such strategies typically fail when there is substantial noise in the reference standard. Additional methods for dealing with within-class heterogeneity would be highly welcome
